userStories.title: Review-pair helper and config comments
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a concurrency eligibility predicate and an all-settled two-review dispatcher while correcting the existing configuration comments.

**Motivation** — `review.adversarial.parallel` and `maxConcurrentSessions` are declared but nothing in `src/` reads them.

**Approach** — A new module, `src/execution/story-orchestrator/review-pair.ts`, runs the two review phases of one story concurrently by calling the existing `runPhase` for each; `runPhase` is unchanged. The pair waits for both reviews to settle and never cancels one review because its sibling failed. A review runs concurrently only when all three hold: `review.adversarial.parallel` is `true`; `review.adversarial.maxConcurrentSessions` is 2 or more (each review is one session, the debate feature having been removed); and both `semantic-review` and `adversarial-review` are among the phases the caller is about to run. Otherwise sequential behaviour is unchanged, including the #1666 rule that a `semantic-review` failure continues to `adversarial-review` in the canonical loop.

**Interface** — verbatim target signatures:
```typescript
// src/execution/story-orchestrator/review-pair.ts
export function shouldRunReviewsConcurrently(
  reviewConfig: { adversarial?: { parallel?: boolean; maxConcurrentSessions?: number } } | undefined,
  phases: readonly InternalPhase[], // the phases the CALLER is about to run
): boolean;

export async function runReviewPair(
  ctx: CallContext,
  pair: readonly [InternalPhase, InternalPhase], // [semantic-review, adversarial-review]
  tracking: PhaseTracking,
  isThreeSession?: boolean,
  progress?: { indices: readonly [number, number]; total: number },
): Promise<void>; // results land in tracking.phaseOutputs / phaseCosts via runPhase

export const _reviewPairDeps: { runPhase: typeof runPhase }; // test seam
```

**Approach** — `shouldRunReviewsConcurrently` returns `true` only when `phases` contains both review phases. An unset `maxConcurrentSessions` resolves to the schema default of `2`. The callers resolve review config as `ctx.config?.review ?? ctx.packageView.config.review` (as `nbf-deps.ts` does) and pass that value to `shouldRunReviewsConcurrently`; `runReviewPair` only receives the call context, pair, tracking, session flag and optional progress. On throwing reviews, wait for both to settle, log "Phase threw unexpected error" once per throwing phase with storyId first, then rethrow the semantic error if both threw; log the concurrent dispatch once at info level under story-orchestrator. Update the comments in `schemas-review.ts` and `review/types.ts` without changing keys, types, defaults or ranges.

**Scope** — In: new review-pair source module, dispatch seam, unit tests, and comment corrections in `schemas-review.ts` and `review/types.ts`. Out: canonical-loop wiring (US-002) and revalidation wiring (US-003); the feature-level exclusions listed separately also apply.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `shouldRunReviewsConcurrently` returns `true` when `review.adversarial.parallel` is `true`, `maxConcurrentSessions` is `2`, and the `phases` argument contains both `semantic-review` and `adversarial-review`.
[unit] `shouldRunReviewsConcurrently` returns `false` when `review.adversarial.parallel` is `false`, for any `maxConcurrentSessions` value.
[unit] `shouldRunReviewsConcurrently` returns `false` when `review.adversarial.parallel` is `true` and `maxConcurrentSessions` is `1`.
[unit] `shouldRunReviewsConcurrently` returns `false` when `reviewConfig` is `undefined`.
[unit] `shouldRunReviewsConcurrently` returns `false` when `reviewConfig.adversarial` is absent.

[unit] `shouldRunReviewsConcurrently` returns `true` when `parallel` is `true`, `maxConcurrentSessions` is `undefined` and `phases` contains both review phases (an unset cap resolves to the schema default of `2`).
[unit] `shouldRunReviewsConcurrently` returns `false` when `phases` contains `semantic-review` but not `adversarial-review`, with `parallel` `true` and `maxConcurrentSessions` `2`.
[unit] `shouldRunReviewsConcurrently` returns `false` when `phases` contains `adversarial-review` but not `semantic-review`, with `parallel` `true` and `maxConcurrentSessions` `2`.
[unit] `runReviewPair` calls `_reviewPairDeps.runPhase` for both `semantic-review` and `adversarial-review` before either call's promise resolves.

[unit] After `runReviewPair` resolves, `tracking.phaseCosts` holds each phase's own cost, with neither phase's cost overwriting the other's.

[unit] When `_reviewPairDeps.runPhase` rejects for `semantic-review` while the `adversarial-review` call is still pending, `runReviewPair` does not settle until the `adversarial-review` call has settled.
[unit] When `_reviewPairDeps.runPhase` rejects for `semantic-review` and `adversarial-review` succeeds, `runReviewPair` rejects with the `semantic-review` error.
[unit] When `_reviewPairDeps.runPhase` rejects for both phases, `runReviewPair` rejects with the `semantic-review` error.

[unit] When `_reviewPairDeps.runPhase` rejects for a phase, `runReviewPair` logs one error "Phase threw unexpected error" with `storyId` as the first key and the throwing `phase` name, once per throwing phase.
[unit] `runReviewPair` logs one info line "Running semantic-review and adversarial-review concurrently" under the `story-orchestrator` stage, with `storyId` as the first key.

routing.reasoning: New concurrent all-settled abstraction and cross-module tracking/logging plus schema and interface comments, but no security enforcement or novel orchestration architecture.

userStories.title: Canonical loop runs the review pair
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Integrate opt-in two-review concurrency into the first-pass canonical loop without changing its signature, resume semantics, or default sequential dispatch.

**Motivation** — The consumer (`canParallelize` in `src/review/orchestrator.ts`) was deleted by f38aedf21 (#1084) and never ported to `runCanonicalLoop`. Setting `parallel: true` is accepted and silently has no effect, so operators expecting wall-clock savings per review round get none.

**Approach** — Baseline: `runCanonicalLoop(plan: PlanParams, tracking: PhaseTracking, orderedPhases: readonly InternalPhase[]): Promise<{ shortCircuitPhase: string | undefined }>` runs every phase strictly in order. Target: the same signature and return shape. When `shouldRunReviewsConcurrently` is true at `semantic-review`, the loop dispatches both reviews through `runReviewPair`, skips the separate `adversarial-review` iteration, then applies the per-phase evaluation the sequential loop applies (see Failure Handling). The caller decides which phases it is about to run. `runCanonicalLoop` passes only phases with no passing entry in `phaseOutputs` (its existing resume skip guard). Otherwise sequential behaviour is unchanged, including the #1666 rule that a `semantic-review` failure continues to `adversarial-review` in the canonical loop. The review config is read as `ctx.config?.review ?? ctx.packageView.config.review` (as `nbf-deps.ts` does).

**Interface** — `runCanonicalLoop(plan: PlanParams, tracking: PhaseTracking, orderedPhases: readonly InternalPhase[]): Promise<{ shortCircuitPhase: string | undefined }>`; call `shouldRunReviewsConcurrently(reviewConfig, runnablePhases)` and `runReviewPair(ctx, [semanticPhase, adversarialPhase], tracking, isThreeSession, { indices: [semanticIndex, adversarialIndex], total: orderedPhases.length })`.

**Approach** — After both settle, evaluate each phase in canonical order: keep the semantic-failed second-opinion warning, record only passing phases green using the existing checkpoint helper, and let adversarial failure override semantic in `shortCircuitPhase` when both fail. If the pair rejects, record green for each review with a passing entry in phaseOutputs in canonical order before propagating the already-logged rejection; do not log the same unexpected error again. Keep the skip-guard read single-threaded before dispatch; passing seeded semantic means only adversarial runs sequentially.

**Scope** — In: first-pass canonical-loop pairing, its existing checkpoint/error/failure behavior, and integration tests using deferred review ops and resume checkpoints. Out: revalidation dispatch (US-003) and mechanical-only resume changes. Concurrent review inside `runPostRectificationResume`; that loop halts on the first failure and grants one extra rectification pass, and both contracts assume sequential phases. Regrouping or renumbering the interleaved `phaseIndex`/`totalPhases` phase-start log lines that the two concurrent reviews emit.

userStories.title: Revalidation sweep runs the review pair
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Dispatch the two reviewers together in eligible post-fix revalidation sweeps and collect both reviewers' findings before short-circuiting.

**Approach** — Baseline: iterates the selected phases one at a time and breaks at the first failed phase. Target: for each phase it calls `dispatchRevalidationPhase`, skips kinds already dispatched in the sweep, and when the pair ran it pushes findings from both reviewers before it applies its short-circuit break. `rectification.ts` is 597 lines against the 600-line limit, so the review-dispatch step lives in the new sibling module `revalidation-reviews.ts`. The revalidation sweep has no skip guard and passes every selected review phase. The ADR-024 non-blocking-fix sweep already excludes both reviews (`nonBlockingExcludePhases()`), so it never pairs. This changes what the fixer receives: today a `semantic-review` failure breaks the sweep before `adversarial-review` is dispatched, so the next fix iteration sees semantic findings only. Under `parallel: true` both reviews run, so the next iteration sees both sets of findings (likely fewer fix rounds) at the price of an adversarial session, and its spend, in rounds where sequential mode would have skipped it. Opting into `parallel: true` accepts that trade-off.

**Interface** — verbatim target signature:
```typescript
// src/execution/story-orchestrator/revalidation-reviews.ts
export async function dispatchRevalidationPhase(
  ctx: CallContext,
  phase: InternalPhase,             // the sweep's current phase
  phases: readonly InternalPhase[], // every phase selected for this sweep, in order
  tracking: PhaseTracking,
  isThreeSession?: boolean,
): Promise<readonly PhaseKind[]>;   // the kinds this call dispatched
```

**Approach** — `dispatchRevalidationPhase` dispatches `phase` through `runPhase`, except when `phase` is `semantic-review` and `shouldRunReviewsConcurrently` is true for `phases`: then it dispatches the pair through `runReviewPair` and returns `["semantic-review", "adversarial-review"]`. Resolve config via `ctx.config?.review ?? ctx.packageView.config.review`. Preserve existing gate carve-outs, NBF triage/quarantine, lite gate-last ordering, early-abort guard, strategy/extra phase selection and postValidate. Collect both review findings (when failing) before breaking on failure, while retaining the old single-phase first-failure break for sequential mode. Keep both `rectification.ts` and the new `revalidation-reviews.ts` within the 600-line source limit; extract the dispatch step instead of expanding the 597-line module in place.

**Scope** — In: new sweep-dispatch module, minimal rectification loop integration, and unit/integration tests through the captured FixCycle validate callback. Out: canonical loop integration (US-002), `runPostRectificationResume`, and any change to how `gatherRectificationFindings` merges findings; the feature-level exclusions listed separately also apply.

When both reviews fail during parallel revalidation, `cycle.validate(...)` returns `shortCircuited: true`.

When `ctx.runtime.signal` is already aborted on entry, `runRectification` returns `{}` before dispatching any review.
[integration] `ExecutionPlan.run()` in lite revalidation mode with `parallel` `true` dispatches `full-suite-gate` after both reviews have resolved.

[unit] `dispatchRevalidationPhase` for any phase with `shouldRunReviewsConcurrently` false returns only that phase's own kind.

routing.reasoning: Adds a sweep-dispatch abstraction to a nearly full source file and integrates all-settled reviews with existing finding extraction and short-circuit behavior.

analysis: Existing TypeScript builder-phase story orchestration; no migration or public config-shape change. src/config/schemas-review.ts:113-118 already declares adversarial.parallel false and maxConcurrentSessions default 2, int range 1–4, but its comments describe Promise.all and a vague cap; src/review/types.ts:245-248 duplicates these declarations in the hand-written interface; the key-drift guard at src/review/types.ts:350-421 must continue to agree with the schema. Per-story effective review config uses ctx.config?.review ?? ctx.packageView.config.review at src/execution/story-orchestrator/nbf-deps.ts:40-43. src/execution/story-orchestrator/types.ts:83-97 and :160-201 define PhaseKind, InternalPhase and CANONICAL_ORDER (semantic immediately before adversarial); :220-259 maps autofix-implementer to both reviews, autofix-test-writer to adversarial only, and full-suite-rectify to both. src/execution/story-orchestrator/phase-state.ts:22-43 assembles configured phases in canonical order. src/execution/story-orchestrator/execution-plan.ts:45-89 wires hydration, canonical loop, rectification and the distinct post-rectification resume. src/execution/story-orchestrator/execution-plan-phases.ts:31-40 defines PlanParams/PhaseTracking, :110-138 implements recordGreenCheckpoint, and :186-252 runs the canonical loop with resume skip guard, sequential runPhase dispatch, #1666 semantic-failure continuation, error logging and green checkpointing. Under concurrent dispatch, compute runnable phases before the pair, dispatch each review once, evaluate in canonical order after both settle, keep shortCircuitPhase semantics (both failures -> adversarial), and checkpoint passing siblings even when the other throws without double-logging. Keep runPostRectificationResume at :268-339 and mechanical-only resume at :351-391 sequential. src/execution/story-orchestrator/run-phase.ts:186-202 has the unchanged runPhase signature; :286-287 stores the callOp result in phaseOutputs keyed by opName, and :386 accumulates phaseCosts keyed by opName in finally. The existing mutable callOp seam is at :39-82; a new _reviewPairDeps.runPhase seam can isolate pair unit tests. Use all-settled semantics rather than rejecting immediately so the sibling finishes, log each thrown phase once through getSafeLogger with storyId first, and prefer the semantic rejection when both reject. Concurrent reviewers have distinct output/cost keys and iteration maps, but reviewer read-only behavior is only a prompt-level assumption; no permission enforcement is introduced. src/execution/story-orchestrator/rectification.ts:215-242 filters review phases for NBF and guards an already-aborted signal; :361-485 is the validate closure, checking abortion before selecting phases via phasesToRevalidate, adding extra phases, moving full-suite-gate last in lite mode, and currently dispatching one runPhase then extracting/filtering findings and short-circuiting on failure. The new sibling revalidation-reviews.ts should own only dispatch selection, with the loop tracking dispatched kinds; collect findings for both dispatched review outputs before deciding the short-circuit, without changing gate carve-out, NBF triage/quarantine, postValidate or gatherRectificationFindings at rectification.ts:64-81. rectification.ts is already 597 lines, so extraction must leave it at or under the 600-line source limit. src/execution/story-orchestrator/phase-eval.ts:20-49 defines phasePassed, :70-96 extracts only failure findings, and :298-331 selects/arranges revalidation phases; src/execution/non-blocking-fix.ts:41-55 excludes both reviews from the NBF sweep. Test fixtures and seams: test/unit/execution/story-orchestrator-revalidation.test.ts:1-148 captures FixCycle via _storyOrchestratorDeps.runFixCycle and calls validate while replacing callOp; test/unit/execution/story-orchestrator-resume-integration.test.ts:1-29 and :135-175 exercise resume and recordGreen; test/unit/execution/story-orchestrator.test.ts:1-42 covers builder dispatch and thrown errors. Use deferred callOp promises in integration tests to prove overlap without real reviewer sessions. Risk: default false and cap 1 must preserve sequential ordering/cost, semantic failure must still allow adversarial on the canonical path but not on the sequential sweep, early gate failure/abort must prevent review dispatch, and progress logs may interleave without renumbering. No data migration: existing config keys/defaults/ranges and runPhase interface stay intact; enable behavior solely by opt-in parallel true with both phases eligible and cap >= 2.
outOfScope: Concurrent review inside `runPostRectificationResume`; that loop halts on the first failure and grants one extra rectification pass, and both contracts assume sequential phases.
Cancelling one review session because its sibling failed or finished first.
Removing the `parallel` or `maxConcurrentSessions` keys, or adding deprecation warnings for them.
Running any phase concurrently other than `semantic-review` with `adversarial-review`.
Enforcing read-only tool permissions for review sessions under the `unrestricted` permission profile.
Counting debate debaters toward `maxConcurrentSessions`; the debate feature was removed.
Any change to how `gatherRectificationFindings` merges or de-duplicates findings from the two reviewers.
Regrouping or renumbering the interleaved `phaseIndex`/`totalPhases` phase-start log lines that the two concurrent reviews emit.
